name: What is the difference between natural stone and porcelain tile for bathroom surfaces?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between natural stone and porcelain tile for bathroom surfaces?

acceptedAnswer.text: Natural stone requires regular sealing to resist water and staining, whereas porcelain tile is non-porous and virtually maintenance-free. Porcelain works exceptionally well in wet shower pans and high-moisture zones because it does not absorb moisture or react to standard bathroom cleaners. Natural stone, such as marble or slate, delivers distinctive organic patterns and texture, but it demands pH-neutral cleaning products and periodic resealing to prevent discoloration and water penetration. If low ongoing maintenance is your priority, porcelain is usually the better choice. If natural aesthetic variation is your goal, stone provides unmatched visual character.
acceptedAnswer.description: Porcelain is non-porous and low-maintenance, while natural stone offers unique textures but requires regular sealing and gentle cleaners to prevent moisture damage.
